paper_metadata.title: Quantum Architecture Search for Quantum Monte Carlo Integration via Conditional Parameterized Circuits with Application to Finance

experiments.description: Genetically trained PQC for a European call option payoff, evaluated as a function approximator and compared against its conditional version and a bitwise quantum arithmetic baseline.

algorithm.variant: Genetic structure learning PQC for European vanilla option payoff
algorithm.ansatz: Custom PQC with data re-uploading and rotational encodings
algorithm.optimizer: PennyLane RMSProp; structure search uses acceptance rule with probability exp(-5(cnew-cold)/cold)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 20 generations with 20 structure-optimization iterations per generation; accept new structure if cost decreases, otherwise accept with probability exp(-5(cnew-cold)/cold)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Single underlying asset price x encoded through rotational gates (RZ/RX/RY) in the PQC; discretized asset values are mapped to basis states in the CPQC variant
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate the European call payoff f+(X)=max(X-K,0) as a quantum model output

problem_instance.description: European call option payoff approximation with strike 100 over discretized asset prices

dataset_specification.description: Asset prices shown in Fig. 3/4 are discretized over the range approximately 70 to 130; the appendix circuit uses 3 control qubits for 8 basis states

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scaled discretization of the underlying asset price into xk in [0,2pi); basis encoding for CPQC
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Function approximation visualized against the true payoff; CPQC compared to PQC and bitwise quantum arithmetic in gate-count/depth plots

implementation_details.transpilation_target: CNOT and U(θ,φ,λ) gate decomposition for resource comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Genetic structure search over PQC blocks; training data from discretized payoff values
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Option price recovered by classical discounting/rescaling; plots compare predicted payoff to truth

classical_baselines.unit: asymptotic rate in number of applications of A

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming efficient state preparation and amplitude estimation subroutine
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper emphasizes that efficient implementation of the function operator is crucial; the speedup is theoretical and depends on circuit efficiency.

experiments.description: Genetically trained PQC for a European basket option with fixed weights, evaluated as a function approximator and compared against its conditional version and a bitwise quantum arithmetic baseline.

algorithm.variant: Genetic structure learning PQC for European basket option with fixed weight
algorithm.ansatz: Custom PQC with data re-uploading and rotational encodings
algorithm.optimizer: PennyLane RMSProp; structure search uses acceptance rule with probability exp(-5(cnew-cold)/cold)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Same genetic procedure as the call option: 20 generations, 20 structure-optimization iterations per generation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two underlying asset prices encoded via rotational gates; CPQC uses basis-encoded control registers for discretized asset values
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate basket payoff fBasket(X)=max(wX-K,0) with fixed weights w=(2/3,1/3)

problem_instance.description: European basket call option with two underlyings and fixed weights

dataset_specification.description: Two underlying securities X=(X(1),X(2)); each underlying represented on a separate qubit register; for the comparison figure, n ranges from 5 to 14 control qubits

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scaled discretization of each underlying; same discretization resolution required for the quantum arithmetic baseline
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Function approximation compared to true basket payoff; resource scaling compared to IBM qiskit finance bitwise implementation

implementation_details.transpilation_target: CNOT and U(θ,φ,λ) gate decomposition for resource comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Genetic structure search over PQC blocks; training data from discretized basket payoff values
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Option price recovered by classical discounting/rescaling; plots compare predicted payoff to truth

classical_baselines.method_name: ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic
ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic

speedup_claims.factor: O(n) gate complexity for CPQC versus O(n log2 n) for quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.baseline_method: ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.conditions: for fixed approximation level and after classical pretraining; resource comparison after CNOT and U(theta,phi,lambda) decomposition
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports the CPQC has 92 CNOTs and depth 151 for n=14, but the baseline is shown only as scaling plots rather than a single numeric value.

experiments.description: Genetically trained PQC for a European basket option with variable weight as an input feature, demonstrating that the weight is encoded only once and can be reused across weights.

algorithm.variant: Genetic structure learning PQC for European basket option with variable weight
algorithm.ansatz: Custom PQC with data re-uploading and rotational encodings
algorithm.optimizer: PennyLane RMSProp; structure search uses acceptance rule with probability exp(-5(cnew-cold)/cold)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Same genetic procedure as the other experiments; trained PQC shown in Fig. A.5

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two asset prices plus the first basket weight are encoded as inputs; the weight feature is encoded once at the start of the circuit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate basket payoff fBasket(X)=max(wX-K,0) for variable weight w

problem_instance.description: European basket call option with two underlyings and variable first-asset weight

dataset_specification.description: Inputs are the two asset prices and the first asset weight; the figure shows three example weights w1=0, w1≈0.37, and w1≈0.74

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scaled discretization of asset prices; weight treated as an additional continuous input feature
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Qualitative comparison of predicted payoff surfaces against the true basket payoff for multiple weights

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Genetic structure search over PQC blocks; training data includes weight as an input feature
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Option price recovered by classical discounting/rescaling; plots compare predicted payoff to truth for different weights

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment is a qualitative function-approximation demonstration; no explicit classical baseline or speedup is reported.

experiments.description: Resource comparison between the paper's CPQC approach and IBM qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic for European vanilla option pricing.

algorithm.variant: Bitwise quantum arithmetic state preparation for option pricing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Underlying asset discretized on n qubits; comparator flips ancilla if Xi > K; payoff encoded via controlled Y rotations
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare amplitude proportional to the European call payoff for use in amplitude estimation

problem_instance.description: European vanilla call option pricing baseline from IBM qiskit finance

dataset_specification.description: Discretized underlying with N=2^n points; comparison shown for control-qubit sizes n from 5 to 25 in Fig. 5

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Scaled discretization of the underlying; comparator and payoff scaling used to build the amplitude for AE
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: CNOT count and depth compared against CPQC after decomposition into CNOT and U(θ,φ,λ) gates

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Comparator circuit and weighted payoff scaling
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Option price recovered by rescaling the measured ancilla probability

speedup_claims.conditions: via amplitude estimation with efficient state preparation
speedup_claims.caveats: This is the baseline method underlying the AE framework; the paper’s comparison here is specifically against the bitwise quantum arithmetic implementation, not a classical numerical benchmark.

experiments.description: Resource comparison between the paper's CPQC approach and IBM qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic for European basket option pricing with fixed weights.

algorithm.variant: Bitwise quantum arithmetic state preparation for basket option pricing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each underlying asset is represented on a separate qubit register; an additional weighted-sum register of size log2(sum wk)+1 is used before the comparator
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare amplitude proportional to the basket payoff max(wX-K,0) for amplitude estimation

problem_instance.description: European basket call option with two underlyings and fixed weights

dataset_specification.description: Two underlyings X=(X(1),X(2)); same discretization required for all securities; comparison shown for control-qubit sizes n from 2 to 14 in Fig. 6

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Weighted sum of discretized underlyings computed before comparator; then vanilla-option methodology applied
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: CNOT count and depth compared against CPQC after decomposition into CNOT and U(θ,φ,λ) gates

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Weighted-sum operator over two asset registers
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Option price recovered by rescaling the measured ancilla probability

speedup_claims.factor: O(n) gate complexity for CPQC versus O(n log2 n) for quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.baseline_method: ibm qiskit finance bitwise quantum arithmetic
speedup_claims.conditions: fixed approximation level; after decomposition into CNOT and U(theta,phi,lambda) gates
